blocks.text: The docker CLI is a thin REST client; dockerd handles the API, builds, networks and volumes; containerd manages images and container lifecycle; a per-container shim parents the process; runc creates namespaces and cgroups, execs the process, and exits.

rows: Sends API calls; holds no state
API, BuildKit, networks, volumes, logging drivers
Image pull/storage, lifecycle; also used directly by Kubernetes
Holds stdio and exit status; decouples containers from daemon restarts
OCI runtime: sets up the container, execs, exits

items: The CLI is remote-capable: `DOCKER_HOST=ssh://...` or `docker context` sends builds (and their context upload) to another host.
Socket access = daemon control = root on the host.
`"live-restore": true` keeps containers running across dockerd restarts because the shim is their parent.
Kubernetes dropped dockershim (v1.24) and talks to containerd/CRI-O; Docker-built images still run because they're OCI.

blocks.text: Q: "What happens when you run docker run?" A: "The CLI calls dockerd's API; the image is pulled if missing; dockerd asks containerd to create the container; containerd starts a shim, which uses runc to set up namespaces, cgroups and the rootfs and exec the entrypoint; runc exits and the shim stays as parent."

items: runc exits after start; the shim keeps the container alive.
The CLI can drive a remote daemon.
Kubernetes doesn't need Docker, only OCI images.
